w: Rila National Park spans 810.46 square kilometres of the Rila mountain range in south-west Bulgaria - the largest national park in the country by area. It covers the range's wild upper reaches, forested slopes rising to open alpine ground, a swath of high country large enough to anchor Bulgaria's park system.
s: Bulgaria's largest national park, 810 sq km of high Rila
_facts: 810.46 sq km, the largest national park in Bulgaria
Covers the wild upper reaches of the Rila range

w: Rila Monastery Nature Park covers 252.535 square kilometres of the western Rila range, between 750m and 2,713m, with 28 glacial lakes, forests and meadows. Created in 1992 within Rila National Park, most land was reassigned in 2000 to Rila Monastery; it draws over a million visitors a year, second only to Vitosha.
s: 252 sq km of forest, meadow and 28 glacial lakes
_facts: 252.535 sq km, altitude 750-2,713m, includes 28 glacial lakes
Most land owned by Rila Monastery since a 2000 reassignment
Over 1 million visitors/year, Bulgaria's second most-visited nature park

a: Southern foothills of Musala, near Samokov
w: Beli Iskar Reservoir sits in the southern foothills of Musala, the Balkans' highest peak, in the Rila range. Built between 1935 and 1945, it is among the oldest and highest-altitude reservoirs in Europe, and today supplies about 20 percent of Sofia's drinking water, alongside the main Iskar Reservoir 75km to the north.
s: A 1930s reservoir supplying a fifth of Sofia's water
_facts: Built 1935-1945, one of Europe's oldest and highest-altitude reservoirs

w: The Musala Lakes are a chain of seven glacial lakes in the Rila mountains, lying between 2,322m and 2,709m on the flanks of Musala - at 2,925m the highest peak in the Balkans. Carved by the ice that shaped Musala's cirque, they sit among the highest standing water in southeastern Europe, a stark string on Rila's flank.
s: Seven glacial lakes beneath the Balkans' tallest peak
_facts: Located on the flanks of Musala (2,925m), the Balkans' highest peak

w: Irechek rises to 2,852m in the eastern Rila mountains, the third-highest summit in the range after Musala and Malka Musala, near the Musala Lakes within the Musala Cirque. It is named for Konstantin Jirecek, the Czech historian who studied Bulgarian history and served the Bulgarian government after 1878.
s: Rila's third-highest peak, named for a Czech historian
_facts: 2,852m, third-highest peak in Rila after Musala and Malka Musala
Named for historian Konstantin Jirecek, who worked for Bulgaria after 1878

a: Central Rila, Rila Monastery Nature Park
w: Ribni Ezera - Fish Lakes - are a cluster of glacial lakes in a cirque in central Rila, within the Rila Monastery Nature Park. The larger Upper Ribno Lake, at 2,227m, runs 800m long and up to 9m deep, fed by some 30 streams. Together with the lower lake, they form the headwaters of the Rilska River.
s: Fish Lakes cirque feeding the Rilska River's headwaters
_facts: Upper Ribno Lake: 2,227m, 800m long, up to 9m deep, fed by ~30 streams
Headwaters of the Rilska River; ~14.5 million cubic metres annual outflow

w: The Ibar reserve was declared in February 1985 within Rila National Park to protect relict plants and rare animal species found in the Rila mountains. Covering 22.62 square kilometres, it is a small pocket of the range set aside to shield species that survive as leftovers from an earlier, colder climate.
s: A 1985 reserve guarding Rila's relict plants
_facts: Declared February 1985, within Rila National Park
22.62 sq km, protects relict plants and rare animal species

w: Rila is Bulgaria's highest mountain range and the highest between the Alps and the Caucasus, its summit Musala reaching 2,925m - the sixth-highest range summit in Europe. Nearly 200 glacial lakes dot its slopes, including the Seven Rila Lakes, and its main ridge forms Bulgaria's Black Sea-Aegean watershed.
s: Bulgaria's highest range, home to the Seven Rila Lakes
_facts: Musala, 2,925m, sixth-highest mountain range summit in Europe
Nearly 200 glacial lakes including the Seven Rila Lakes
Watershed divide between Black Sea and Aegean drainage; source of the Maritsa and Iskar rivers
